name: lists
description: List utilities beyond the builtins: windows, splits, grouping, zips, set operations, combinatorics, searching and safe index edits

api.name: split_at
api.sig: fn split_at[A](xs: List[A], i: Int) -> (List[A], List[A])
api.doc:
`(xs.take(i), xs.drop(i))` with `i` clamped to `0..=xs.len`: a negative `i` gives `([], xs)`
and an `i` past the end gives `(xs, [])`.

api.name: split_while
api.sig: fn split_while[A, e](xs: List[A], p: A -> Bool ! e) -> (List[A], List[A]) ! e
api.doc:
The longest prefix whose elements all satisfy `p`, and the rest (Haskell's `span`). `p` is
called once per element of the prefix, plus once for the first element that fails.

api.name: split_until
api.sig: fn split_until[A, e](xs: List[A], p: A -> Bool ! e) -> (List[A], List[A]) ! e
api.doc:
The longest prefix with no element satisfying `p`, and the rest, which starts with the first
element that does (Haskell's `break`).

api.name: split_when
api.sig: fn split_when[A, e](xs: List[A], p: (A, A) -> Bool ! e) -> List[List[A]] ! e
api.doc:
Splits `xs` between every pair of neighbours `a, b` for which `p(a, b)` holds; no element is
lost. An empty list gives `[]`. `split_when([1, 2, 4, 5], (a, b) => b != a + 1)` is
`[[1, 2], [4, 5]]`.

api.name: split_on
api.sig: fn split_on[A](xs: List[A], sep: A) -> List[List[A]]
api.doc:
Splits `xs` at every element equal to `sep`, dropping the separators, like `Str.split`:
`[]` gives `[[]]`, and neighbouring or trailing separators give empty pieces, so the result
always has one more piece than there are separators.

api.name: split_where
api.sig: fn split_where[A, e](xs: List[A], p: A -> Bool ! e) -> List[List[A]] ! e
api.doc: `split_on` with a predicate: splits at every element satisfying `p` and drops those elements.

api.name: split_parts
api.sig: fn split_parts[A](xs: List[A], n: Int where _ >= 1) -> List[List[A]]
api.doc:
Exactly `n` consecutive parts whose lengths differ by at most one, the longer parts first
(more-itertools' `divide`). With fewer than `n` elements the last parts are empty.

api.name: sliding
api.sig: fn sliding[A](xs: List[A], size: Int where _ >= 1, step: Int where _ >= 1, partial: Bool) -> List[List[A]]
api.doc:
Windows of `size` elements starting every `step` elements (Kotlin's `windowed`). With
`partial` false only full windows are returned; with `partial` true the windows that start
before the end but run past it are kept, shortened. `sliding(xs, n, 1, false)` is
`xs.windows(n)` and `sliding(xs, n, n, true)` is `xs.chunks(n)`.

api.name: chunks_padded
api.sig: fn chunks_padded[A](xs: List[A], n: Int where _ >= 1, fill: A) -> List[List[A]]
api.doc: `xs.chunks(n)` with the last chunk padded with `fill` to `n` elements. An empty list gives `[]`.

api.name: chunk_by
api.sig: fn chunk_by[A, K, e](xs: List[A], key: A -> K ! e) -> List[(K, List[A])] ! e
api.doc:
Groups runs of consecutive elements with the same key, each with its key (Python's
`itertools.groupby`, Rust's `chunk_by`). `key` is called once per element. Equal keys that
are not adjacent make separate runs; use `group_into` to group them all.

api.name: rle
api.sig: fn rle[A](xs: List[A]) -> List[(A, Int)]
api.doc: Run-length encoding: each run of equal neighbours as `(value, length)`.

api.name: rle_decode
api.sig: fn rle_decode[A](runs: List[(A, Int)]) -> List[A]
api.doc: The inverse of `rle`; counts below 1 contribute nothing.

api.name: tails
api.sig: fn tails[A](xs: List[A]) -> List[List[A]]
api.doc: Every suffix of `xs`, longest first, ending with `[]`: `xs.len + 1` lists.

api.name: inits
api.sig: fn inits[A](xs: List[A]) -> List[List[A]]
api.doc: Every prefix of `xs`, shortest first, starting with `[]`: `xs.len + 1` lists.

api.name: take_last
api.sig: fn take_last[A](xs: List[A], n: Int) -> List[A]
api.doc: The last `n` elements (all of them when `n >= xs.len`, none when `n <= 0`).

api.name: drop_last
api.sig: fn drop_last[A](xs: List[A], n: Int) -> List[A]
api.doc: `xs` without its last `n` elements (`[]` when `n >= xs.len`, `xs` when `n <= 0`).

api.name: take_last_while
api.sig: fn take_last_while[A, e](xs: List[A], p: A -> Bool ! e) -> List[A] ! e
api.doc: The longest suffix whose elements all satisfy `p`, tested from the end.

api.name: drop_last_while
api.sig: fn drop_last_while[A, e](xs: List[A], p: A -> Bool ! e) -> List[A] ! e
api.doc: `xs` without the longest suffix whose elements all satisfy `p` (an `rstrip` for lists).

api.name: pad_to
api.sig: fn pad_to[A](xs: List[A], n: Int, fill: A) -> List[A]
api.doc: `xs` padded at the end with `fill` to at least `n` elements; longer lists are unchanged.

api.name: pad_front_to
api.sig: fn pad_front_to[A](xs: List[A], n: Int, fill: A) -> List[A]
api.doc: `xs` padded at the front with `fill` to at least `n` elements; longer lists are unchanged.

api.name: dedup
api.sig: fn dedup[A](xs: List[A]) -> List[A]
api.doc:
`xs` with runs of equal neighbours collapsed to their first element (Unix `uniq`). Use the
builtin `unique` to drop every repeat.

api.name: dedup_by
api.sig: fn dedup_by[A, K, e](xs: List[A], key: A -> K ! e) -> List[A] ! e
api.doc: `dedup` comparing keys: keeps the first element of each run of neighbours with equal keys.

api.name: distinct_by
api.sig: fn distinct_by[A, K, e](xs: List[A], key: A -> K ! e) -> List[A] ! e
api.doc:
The first element for each distinct key, in input order (lodash's `uniqBy`). `key` is called
once per element.

api.name: duplicates
api.sig: fn duplicates[A](xs: List[A]) -> List[A]
api.doc: The values that occur more than once, each once, in the order of their first occurrence.

api.name: all_equal
api.sig: fn all_equal[A](xs: List[A]) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether every element equals the first (true for an empty list).

api.name: all_distinct
api.sig: fn all_distinct[A](xs: List[A]) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether no two elements are equal (true for an empty list).

api.name: single
api.sig: fn single[A](xs: List[A]) -> Opt[A]
api.doc: The only element of `xs`, or `none` when it has zero or several.

api.name: frequencies
api.sig: fn frequencies[A](xs: List[A]) -> Map[A, Int]
api.doc:
How many times each value occurs (Python's `Counter`). The builtin `counts` gives the same
numbers as a list in first-seen order.

api.name: count_by
api.sig: fn count_by[A, K, e](xs: List[A], key: A -> K ! e) -> Map[K, Int] ! e
api.doc: How many elements have each key (lodash's `countBy`).

api.name: count_where
api.sig: fn count_where[A, e](xs: List[A], p: A -> Bool ! e) -> Int ! e
api.doc: How many elements satisfy `p`.

api.name: index_by
api.sig: fn index_by[A, K, e](xs: List[A], key: A -> K ! e) -> Map[K, A] ! e
api.doc:
A map from each element's key to the element (lodash's `keyBy`). When several elements share
a key the last one wins; use `group_into` to keep them all.

api.name: associate
api.sig: fn associate[A, K, V, e](xs: List[A], f: A -> (K, V) ! e) -> Map[K, V] ! e
api.doc:
A map built from the `(key, value)` pair `f` gives for each element (Kotlin's `associate`).
When keys repeat the last pair wins.

api.name: group_into
api.sig: fn group_into[A, K, e](xs: List[A], key: A -> K ! e) -> Map[K, List[A]] ! e
api.doc:
The elements grouped by key into a map; each group keeps input order. The builtin `group_by`
gives the same groups as a list in first-seen key order.

api.name: sum_by
api.sig: fn sum_by[A, e](xs: List[A], f: A -> Int ! e) -> Int ! e
api.doc: The sum of `f` over the elements (0 for an empty list); overflow traps like `+`.

api.name: sum_by_f64
api.sig: fn sum_by_f64[A, e](xs: List[A], f: A -> F64 ! e) -> F64 ! e
api.doc:
The sum of `f` over the elements as floats (0.0 for an empty list), with Kahan-Babuska
compensation, so long sums of small terms lose no precision to a large running total.

api.name: min_by
api.sig: fn min_by[A, K: Ord, e](xs: List[A], key: A -> K ! e) -> Opt[A] ! e
api.doc:
The first element with the smallest key, or `none` for an empty list. `key` is called once
per element.

api.name: max_by
api.sig: fn max_by[A, K: Ord, e](xs: List[A], key: A -> K ! e) -> Opt[A] ! e
api.doc:
The first element with the largest key, or `none` for an empty list. `key` is called once per
element.

api.name: min_max
api.sig: fn min_max[T: Ord](xs: List[T]) -> Opt[(T, T)]
api.doc:
The smallest and the largest element in one pass (the first of each among equals), or
`none` for an empty list.

api.name: min_max_by
api.sig: fn min_max_by[A, K: Ord, e](xs: List[A], key: A -> K ! e) -> Opt[(A, A)] ! e
api.doc:
`min_by` and `max_by` in one pass: the first element with the smallest key and the first with
the largest, or `none` for an empty list.

api.name: top_k
api.sig: fn top_k[A, K: Ord, e](xs: List[A], k: Int, key: A -> K ! e) -> List[A] ! e
api.doc:
The `k` elements with the largest keys, largest first; equal keys keep input order, so the
result is stable. `k <= 0` gives `[]` and `k >= xs.len` sorts the whole list.

api.name: bottom_k
api.sig: fn bottom_k[A, K: Ord, e](xs: List[A], k: Int, key: A -> K ! e) -> List[A] ! e
api.doc: The `k` elements with the smallest keys, smallest first, stable like `top_k`.

api.name: largest
api.sig: fn largest[T: Ord](xs: List[T], k: Int) -> List[T]
api.doc: The `k` largest elements, largest first (Python's `heapq.nlargest`).

api.name: smallest
api.sig: fn smallest[T: Ord](xs: List[T], k: Int) -> List[T]
api.doc: The `k` smallest elements, smallest first (Python's `heapq.nsmallest`).

api.name: interleave
api.sig: fn interleave[A](xs: List[A], ys: List[A]) -> List[A]
api.doc: Alternates elements of `xs` and `ys`, starting with `xs`; the rest of the longer list follows.

api.name: interleave_all
api.sig: fn interleave_all[A](xss: List[List[A]]) -> List[A]
api.doc:
Round-robin over any number of lists: the first element of each, then the second of each,
skipping lists that have run out (more-itertools' `interleave_longest`).

api.name: intersperse
api.sig: fn intersperse[A](xs: List[A], sep: A) -> List[A]
api.doc: `sep` between every two elements: `[a, sep, b, sep, c]`.

api.name: intercalate
api.sig: fn intercalate[A](xss: List[List[A]], sep: List[A]) -> List[A]
api.doc: The lists of `xss` joined with `sep` between every two (`join` for lists of lists).

api.name: zip3
api.sig: fn zip3[A, B, C](xs: List[A], ys: List[B], zs: List[C]) -> List[(A, B, C)]
api.doc: Triples of the elements at the same index, as long as the shortest list.

api.name: zip_with
api.sig: fn zip_with[A, B, C, e](xs: List[A], ys: List[B], f: (A, B) -> C ! e) -> List[C] ! e
api.doc: `f` applied to the elements at the same index, as long as the shorter list.

api.name: zip_longest
api.sig: fn zip_longest[A, B](xs: List[A], ys: List[B], fill_a: A, fill_b: B) -> List[(A, B)]
api.doc:
Pairs as long as the longer list, the shorter one padded with its fill value (Python's
`zip_longest`).

api.name: zip_longest_opt
api.sig: fn zip_longest_opt[A, B](xs: List[A], ys: List[B]) -> List[(Opt[A], Opt[B])]
api.doc: Pairs as long as the longer list, with `none` where a list has run out.

api.name: unzip
api.sig: fn unzip[A, B](ps: List[(A, B)]) -> (List[A], List[B])
api.doc: The firsts and the seconds of a list of pairs.

api.name: unzip3
api.sig: fn unzip3[A, B, C](ts: List[(A, B, C)]) -> (List[A], List[B], List[C])
api.doc: The three components of a list of triples.

api.name: transpose
api.sig: fn transpose[A](rows: List[List[A]]) -> List[List[A]]
api.doc:
Rows become columns. Ragged input is allowed: column `i` holds element `i` of every row that
has one, in row order, so it is shorter than the row count when some rows are short, and there
are as many columns as the longest row has elements. `[]` gives `[]`.

api.name: pairwise
api.sig: fn pairwise[A](xs: List[A]) -> List[(A, A)]
api.doc: Adjacent pairs: `[(x0, x1), (x1, x2), ...]`, empty for fewer than two elements.

api.name: combinatorics_limit
api.sig: fn combinatorics_limit() -> Int
api.doc:
The most lists or pairs the combinatoric functions return: 1,000,000. Their `pre` clauses
reject inputs whose output would be larger, so a typo can't ask for a trillion permutations.

api.name: cartesian
api.sig: fn cartesian[A, B](xs: List[A], ys: List[B]) -> List[(A, B)]
api.doc:
Every pair `(x, y)` with `x` from `xs` and `y` from `ys`, `x` varying slowest. At most
`combinatorics_limit()` pairs.

api.name: cartesian_all
api.sig: fn cartesian_all[A](xss: List[List[A]]) -> List[List[A]]
api.doc:
The n-ary cartesian product (Python's `itertools.product`): every list taking one element from
each list of `xss`, the last varying fastest. `[]` gives `[[]]`, and any empty list gives `[]`.
At most `combinatorics_limit()` lists.

api.name: permutations
api.sig: fn permutations[A](xs: List[A], k: Int where _ >= 0) -> List[List[A]]
api.doc:
The `k`-permutations of `xs` by position, in lexicographic order of positions (Python's
`itertools.permutations(xs, k)`): `n! / (n - k)!` lists, `[[]]` for `k == 0` and `[]` for
`k > xs.len`. Equal elements are treated as distinct. At most `combinatorics_limit()` lists.

api.name: combinations
api.sig: fn combinations[A](xs: List[A], k: Int where _ >= 0) -> List[List[A]]
api.doc:
The `k`-combinations of `xs` by position, in lexicographic order of positions, each in input
order (Python's `itertools.combinations`): `C(n, k)` lists, `[[]]` for `k == 0` and `[]` for
`k > xs.len`. At most `combinatorics_limit()` lists.

api.name: combinations_with_replacement
api.sig: fn combinations_with_replacement[A](xs: List[A], k: Int where _ >= 0) -> List[List[A]]
api.doc:
The `k`-combinations with repetition (Python's `combinations_with_replacement`): `C(n + k - 1,
k)` lists in lexicographic order of positions; `[[]]` for `k == 0`, `[]` for an empty `xs`
and `k > 0`. At most `combinatorics_limit()` lists.

api.name: power_set
api.sig: fn power_set[A](xs: List[A]) -> List[List[A]]
api.doc:
Every sublist of `xs` (keeping input order), by size and then lexicographically by position:
`2 ** xs.len` lists, starting with `[]`. At most 20 elements (1,048,576 lists).

api.name: count_permutations
api.sig: fn count_permutations(n: Int, k: Int) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc:
The number of `k`-permutations of `n` items, `n! / (n - k)!` (0 when `k > n`), or `none` when
it doesn't fit in an `Int` or an argument is negative.

api.name: count_combinations
api.sig: fn count_combinations(n: Int, k: Int) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc:
The number of `k`-combinations of `n` items, the binomial coefficient (0 when `k > n`), or
`none` when it doesn't fit in an `Int` or an argument is negative.

api.name: replicate
api.sig: fn replicate[A](x: A, n: Int) -> List[A]
api.doc: A list of `n` copies of `x` (`[]` when `n <= 0`).

api.name: cycle
api.sig: fn cycle[A](xs: List[A], n: Int) -> List[A]
api.doc: `xs` repeated `n` times (`[]` when `n <= 0`).

api.name: cycle_take
api.sig: fn cycle_take[A](xs: List[A], n: Int) -> List[A]
api.doc: The first `n` elements of `xs` repeated forever (`[]` when `xs` is empty or `n <= 0`).

api.name: map_indexed
api.sig: fn map_indexed[A, B, e](xs: List[A], f: (Int, A) -> B ! e) -> List[B] ! e
api.doc: `f(i, x)` for each element and its index.

api.name: filter_indexed
api.sig: fn filter_indexed[A, e](xs: List[A], p: (Int, A) -> Bool ! e) -> List[A] ! e
api.doc: The elements for which `p(i, x)` holds, with `i` the index.

api.name: filter_map
api.sig: fn filter_map[A, B, e](xs: List[A], f: A -> Opt[B] ! e) -> List[B] ! e
api.doc: The values of `f` that are `some`, in order (Rust's `filter_map`).

api.name: compact
api.sig: fn compact[A](xs: List[Opt[A]]) -> List[A]
api.doc: The values inside the `some`s, in order.

api.name: find_map
api.sig: fn find_map[A, B, e](xs: List[A], f: A -> Opt[B] ! e) -> Opt[B] ! e
api.doc: The first `some` that `f` gives, calling `f` only until then (Rust's `find_map`).

api.name: partition_map
api.sig: fn partition_map[A, B, C, e](xs: List[A], f: A -> Res[B, C] ! e) -> (List[B], List[C]) ! e
api.doc: The `ok` values and the `err` values of `f`, each in order.

api.name: partition_results
api.sig: fn partition_results[B, C](rs: List[Res[B, C]]) -> (List[B], List[C])
api.doc: The `ok` values and the `err` values, each in order.

api.name: sequence_opt
api.sig: fn sequence_opt[A](xs: List[Opt[A]]) -> Opt[List[A]]
api.doc: `some` of every value when all are `some`, else `none`.

api.name: sequence_res
api.sig: fn sequence_res[A, E](rs: List[Res[A, E]]) -> Res[List[A], E]
api.doc: `ok` of every value when all are `ok`, else the first `err`.

api.name: at
api.sig: fn at[A](xs: List[A], i: Int) -> Opt[A]
api.doc:
The element at `i`, counting from the end when `i` is negative (`-1` is the last), or `none`
when out of range.

api.name: insert_at
api.sig: fn insert_at[A](xs: List[A], i: Int, x: A) -> List[A]
api.doc:
`xs` with `x` inserted before index `i`; `i` is clamped to `0..=xs.len`, so a negative `i`
inserts at the front and one past the end appends.

api.name: insert_all_at
api.sig: fn insert_all_at[A](xs: List[A], i: Int, ys: List[A]) -> List[A]
api.doc: `xs` with all of `ys` inserted before index `i`, clamped like `insert_at`.

api.name: remove_at
api.sig: fn remove_at[A](xs: List[A], i: Int) -> List[A]
api.doc: `xs` without the element at `i`; an out-of-range `i` (negative included) leaves it unchanged.

api.name: remove_first
api.sig: fn remove_first[A](xs: List[A], x: A) -> List[A]
api.doc:
`xs` without the first element equal to `x` (unchanged when there is none). The builtin
`filter` removes them all.

api.name: set_at
api.sig: fn set_at[A](xs: List[A], i: Int, x: A) -> List[A]
api.doc: `xs` with the element at `i` replaced by `x`; out of range leaves it unchanged.

api.name: update_at
api.sig: fn update_at[A, e](xs: List[A], i: Int, f: A -> A ! e) -> List[A] ! e
api.doc:
`xs` with the element at `i` replaced by `f` of it; out of range leaves it unchanged and
doesn't call `f`.

api.name: swap
api.sig: fn swap[A](xs: List[A], i: Int, j: Int) -> List[A]
api.doc: `xs` with the elements at `i` and `j` exchanged; unchanged when either is out of range.

api.name: move_item
api.sig: fn move_item[A](xs: List[A], from: Int, to: Int) -> List[A]
api.doc:
`xs` with the element at `from` moved so that it ends at index `to` (clamped to the valid
range); unchanged when `from` is out of range.

api.name: find_last
api.sig: fn find_last[A, e](xs: List[A], p: A -> Bool ! e) -> Opt[A] ! e
api.doc: The last element satisfying `p`, testing from the end.

api.name: find_last_index
api.sig: fn find_last_index[A, e](xs: List[A], p: A -> Bool ! e) -> Opt[Int] ! e
api.doc: The index of the last element satisfying `p`, testing from the end.

api.name: last_index_of
api.sig: fn last_index_of[A](xs: List[A], x: A) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc: The index of the last element equal to `x`.

api.name: indices_where
api.sig: fn indices_where[A, e](xs: List[A], p: A -> Bool ! e) -> List[Int] ! e
api.doc: The indexes of every element satisfying `p`, ascending.

api.name: indices_of
api.sig: fn indices_of[A](xs: List[A], x: A) -> List[Int]
api.doc: The indexes of every element equal to `x`, ascending.

api.name: partition_point
api.sig: fn partition_point[A, e](xs: List[A], p: A -> Bool ! e) -> Int ! e
api.doc:
The first index at which `p` is false, for a list that is partitioned (every element
satisfying `p` comes before every one that doesn't); `xs.len` when `p` holds everywhere.
Binary search: `p` is called O(log n) times.

api.name: lower_bound_by
api.sig: fn lower_bound_by[A, K: Ord, e](xs: List[A], key: A -> K ! e, target: K) -> Int ! e
api.doc: The first index whose key is at least `target`, in a list sorted by `key` (`xs.len` if none).

api.name: upper_bound_by
api.sig: fn upper_bound_by[A, K: Ord, e](xs: List[A], key: A -> K ! e, target: K) -> Int ! e
api.doc:
The first index whose key is greater than `target`, in a list sorted by `key` (`xs.len` if
none).

api.name: binary_search_by
api.sig: fn binary_search_by[A, K: Ord, e](xs: List[A], key: A -> K ! e, target: K) -> Opt[Int] ! e
api.doc: The first index whose key equals `target` in a list sorted by `key`, or `none`.

api.name: insert_sorted
api.sig: fn insert_sorted[T: Ord](xs: List[T], x: T) -> List[T]
api.doc:
`x` inserted into the sorted list `xs` after any equal elements, so the list stays sorted and
insertion is stable.

api.name: insert_sorted_by
api.sig: fn insert_sorted_by[A, K: Ord, e](xs: List[A], x: A, key: A -> K ! e) -> List[A] ! e
api.doc: `x` inserted into `xs`, sorted by `key`, after any elements with an equal key.

api.name: index_of_sublist
api.sig: fn index_of_sublist[A](xs: List[A], sub: List[A]) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc:
The first index at which `sub` occurs in `xs` as a contiguous run; `some(0)` for an empty
`sub`. Worst case O(xs.len * sub.len).

api.name: last_index_of_sublist
api.sig: fn last_index_of_sublist[A](xs: List[A], sub: List[A]) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc: The last index at which `sub` occurs in `xs`; `some(xs.len)` for an empty `sub`.

api.name: contains_sublist
api.sig: fn contains_sublist[A](xs: List[A], sub: List[A]) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `sub` occurs in `xs` as a contiguous run (always for an empty `sub`).

api.name: has_prefix
api.sig: fn has_prefix[A](xs: List[A], prefix: List[A]) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `xs` starts with `prefix`.

api.name: has_suffix
api.sig: fn has_suffix[A](xs: List[A], suffix: List[A]) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `xs` ends with `suffix`.

api.name: count_sublist
api.sig: fn count_sublist[A](xs: List[A], sub: List[A]) -> Int
api.doc:
How many times `sub` occurs in `xs` without overlapping, scanning left to right (like
`Str.count` in Python). An empty `sub` counts `xs.len + 1` times.

api.name: replace_sublist
api.sig: fn replace_sublist[A](xs: List[A], sub: List[A], by: List[A]) -> List[A]
api.doc:
`xs` with every non-overlapping occurrence of `sub` (left to right) replaced by `by`. An empty
`sub` leaves `xs` unchanged.

api.name: fold_right
api.sig: fn fold_right[A, B, e](xs: List[A], init: B, f: (A, B) -> B ! e) -> B ! e
api.doc: Folds from the right: `f(x0, f(x1, ... f(xn, init)))`.

api.name: reduce
api.sig: fn reduce[A, e](xs: List[A], f: (A, A) -> A ! e) -> Opt[A] ! e
api.doc: Folds from the left with the first element as the start, or `none` for an empty list.

api.name: reduce_right
api.sig: fn reduce_right[A, e](xs: List[A], f: (A, A) -> A ! e) -> Opt[A] ! e
api.doc: Folds from the right with the last element as the start, or `none` for an empty list.

api.name: scan_right
api.sig: fn scan_right[A, B, e](xs: List[A], init: B, f: (A, B) -> B ! e) -> List[B] ! e
api.doc:
The accumulators of `fold_right`, aligned with the elements: element `i` of the result is
`f(xs[i], result[i + 1])`, the last one `f(xs[n - 1], init)`. Same length as `xs`, like the
builtin `scan`.

api.name: is_sorted
api.sig: fn is_sorted[T: Ord](xs: List[T]) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether every element is at most the next one.

api.name: is_strictly_sorted
api.sig: fn is_strictly_sorted[T: Ord](xs: List[T]) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether every element is less than the next one (sorted, no repeats).

api.name: is_sorted_by
api.sig: fn is_sorted_by[A, K: Ord, e](xs: List[A], key: A -> K ! e) -> Bool ! e
api.doc: Whether the keys never decrease. `key` is called once per element.

api.name: is_sorted_with
api.sig: fn is_sorted_with[A, e](xs: List[A], cmp: (A, A) -> Int ! e) -> Bool ! e
api.doc: Whether `cmp(a, b) <= 0` for every pair of neighbours, with a comparator like `sort_with`'s.

api.name: argsort
api.sig: fn argsort[T: Ord](xs: List[T]) -> List[Int]
api.doc:
The indexes that sort `xs` (stable: equal elements keep input order), NumPy's `argsort`.
`argsort(xs).map(i => xs[i])` is `xs` sorted.

api.name: argsort_by
api.sig: fn argsort_by[A, K: Ord, e](xs: List[A], key: A -> K ! e) -> List[Int] ! e
api.doc: The indexes that sort `xs` by `key`, stable. `key` is called once per element.

api.name: ranks
api.sig: fn ranks[T: Ord](xs: List[T]) -> List[Int]
api.doc:
The 0-based position of each element in the stable sort (ordinal ranks: ties get consecutive
ranks in input order). The inverse permutation of `argsort`.

api.name: dense_ranks
api.sig: fn dense_ranks[T: Ord](xs: List[T]) -> List[Int]
api.doc:
Dense ranks: 0 for the smallest value, and one more for each larger distinct value; equal
elements share a rank.

api.name: compare_lists
api.sig: fn compare_lists[T: Ord](xs: List[T], ys: List[T]) -> Int
api.doc: Lexicographic comparison by the elements' `Ord`: -1, 0 or 1. A proper prefix comes first.

api.name: merge_by
api.sig: fn merge_by[A, K: Ord, e](xs: List[A], ys: List[A], key: A -> K ! e) -> List[A] ! e
api.doc:
The elements of the sorted lists `xs` and `ys` in one sorted list, by `key`; on equal keys
elements of `xs` come first. The builtin `merge` does this for the elements themselves.

api.name: merge_all
api.sig: fn merge_all[T: Ord](xss: List[List[T]]) -> List[T]
api.doc:
A k-way merge: every element of the lists in one sorted list, stable (on equals, earlier
lists first). With sorted inputs this is the merge; any input gives a sorted result.

api.name: union
api.sig: fn union[A](xs: List[A], ys: List[A]) -> List[A]
api.doc:
The distinct elements of `xs` and then of `ys` that are not in `xs`, each once, in first-seen
order.

api.name: intersect
api.sig: fn intersect[A](xs: List[A], ys: List[A]) -> List[A]
api.doc: The distinct elements of `xs` that also occur in `ys`, in `xs` order.

api.name: difference
api.sig: fn difference[A](xs: List[A], ys: List[A]) -> List[A]
api.doc: The distinct elements of `xs` that don't occur in `ys`, in `xs` order.

api.name: sym_difference
api.sig: fn sym_difference[A](xs: List[A], ys: List[A]) -> List[A]
api.doc: The distinct elements in exactly one of the lists: those of `xs` first, then those of `ys`.

api.name: contains_all
api.sig: fn contains_all[A](xs: List[A], ys: List[A]) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether every element of `ys` occurs in `xs` (true for an empty `ys`).

api.name: contains_any
api.sig: fn contains_any[A](xs: List[A], ys: List[A]) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether some element of `ys` occurs in `xs` (false for an empty `ys`).

api.name: is_disjoint
api.sig: fn is_disjoint[A](xs: List[A], ys: List[A]) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether the lists have no element in common.

api.name: multi_intersect
api.sig: fn multi_intersect[A](xs: List[A], ys: List[A]) -> List[A]
api.doc:
The multiset intersection, keeping duplicates: each value as many times as it occurs in both
lists (the smaller count), in `xs` order.

api.name: multi_difference
api.sig: fn multi_difference[A](xs: List[A], ys: List[A]) -> List[A]
api.doc:
The multiset difference: `xs` with one occurrence removed for each occurrence in `ys`, the
earliest first (Python's `Counter` subtraction, keeping order).

api.name: multi_union
api.sig: fn multi_union[A](xs: List[A], ys: List[A]) -> List[A]
api.doc:
The multiset union: all of `xs`, then the occurrences in `ys` beyond those in `xs` (each value
as many times as the larger count).

api.name: is_permutation
api.sig: fn is_permutation[A](xs: List[A], ys: List[A]) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `ys` is a permutation of `xs`: the same elements with the same counts.

api.name: sample
api.sig: fn sample[A](xs: List[A], k: Int, seed: Int) -> List[A]
api.doc:
`k` distinct positions of `xs` chosen uniformly at random, in random order (Python's
`random.sample`), as a pure function of `seed` like the builtin `shuffle`. `k` is clamped to
`0..=xs.len`.

api.name: sample_ordered
api.sig: fn sample_ordered[A](xs: List[A], k: Int, seed: Int) -> List[A]
api.doc: `sample`, with the chosen elements in their input order.
